resources.string: No music player seen yet. Play music in one, and it is listed here and in %1$s.
No player is switched on. Switch on the players you want Sleevesight to follow in %1$s.
Opens Settings: the players Sleevesight follows, which sources it looks up, your AI service and the API keys, genres, when insights are written, history, and how the app looks (theme, font, layout).
The player Sleevesight follows, and whether it is playing. A tap opens the player.

The track’s genres, from MusicBrainz or Last.fm, behind the Genres button. A tap on one shows which of the track, the artist and the album carry it and where the label comes from; what the genre is, where Wikipedia has an article on it; and, where your AI service can explain it, Why is this …?, a paid call.
A few sentences about the track, written by your AI service from what the sources found, and checked against them.
Each sentence names the source lines it rests on. A tap on one opens Sources at that line. A dimmed sentence rests on none.

Write insight has your AI service write the insight, a paid call on your key. The arrow beside it chooses when insights are written: On demand, On track change (auto) or On track skip (auto). Once an insight is written, it also offers Look again, which looks every source up afresh without an AI call (a paid search on your Exa key when Exa web search is on); when they found something new, Rewrite insight writes the insight from it.

What each source found about the track. A tap opens a table of the sources, each with what it found, and under it the lines they found, each with a link to where it was found. A tap on a source’s letter shows or hides its lines.
